title: Economics Test 2 (Banking, Budget & Schemes — most probable)

questions.q: The Union Budget is presented in Parliament as the 'Annual Financial Statement' under Article:
questions.explain: Article 112 requires the government to present the Annual Financial Statement — the Budget — before Parliament every year.

questions.q: Fiscal deficit of the government means:
options: Total expenditure minus total receipts excluding borrowings
questions.explain: Fiscal deficit shows the government's total borrowing need for the year, because spending exceeds all non-borrowed income.

questions.q: Revenue deficit means:
options: Tax collection falls for one month
questions.explain: A revenue deficit shows the government is borrowing even for day-to-day running expenses.

questions.q: Primary deficit is calculated as fiscal deficit minus:
questions.explain: Primary deficit = fiscal deficit − interest payments on past loans; it shows the current year's borrowing apart from old interest burden.

questions.q: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act was passed mainly to:
options: Keep government deficits and debt under control
Introduce the Goods and Services Tax (GST)
questions.explain: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act, 2003 sets targets so that government borrowing stays within disciplined limits.

questions.q: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was launched in India on:
questions.explain: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) created 'one nation, one tax' by absorbing excise duty, service tax and state Value Added Tax (VAT).

questions.q: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was introduced through which Constitutional Amendment?
questions.explain: The 101st Amendment, 2016 gave both the Centre and the States the power to levy the Goods and Services Tax (GST).

questions.q: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council is chaired by the:
options: Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
questions.explain: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council, with finance ministers of all states as members, decides tax rates and rules.

questions.q: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) in India is a:
questions.explain: Under the Goods and Services Tax (GST), tax is collected where goods and services are consumed, not where they are produced.

questions.q: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council is set up under Article:
questions.explain: Article 279A (added by the 101st Amendment) creates the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council; Article 280 is the Finance Commission.

questions.q: Which of the following is a direct tax?
questions.explain: A direct tax is paid by the person on whom it is imposed — income tax and corporation tax; indirect taxes are passed on to buyers.

questions.q: Customs duty is a tax levied on:
options: Goods imported into and exported out of a country
questions.explain: Customs duty is an indirect tax charged at the border on trade in goods.

questions.q: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is the regulator of:
questions.explain: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) protects investors in the share market; insurance is regulated by the insurance regulator and banks by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).

questions.q: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) was given statutory (legal) powers in the year:
questions.explain: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) was set up in 1988 and made a statutory body through an Act in 1992.

questions.q: The headquarters of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is at:
questions.explain: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) works from Mumbai, India's financial capital.

questions.q: The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) was established in the year:
questions.explain: The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) was set up in 1982 to finance agriculture and rural development.

questions.q: The main function of the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) is to:
options: Provide and regulate credit for agriculture and rural development
questions.explain: The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) refinances rural banks and supports farm and village industries.

questions.q: The Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) mainly provides finance to:
questions.explain: The Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI), set up in 1990, is the main financial institution for small industries.

questions.q: The Export-Import Bank of India (EXIM Bank) mainly finances:
questions.explain: The Export-Import Bank of India (EXIM Bank), set up in 1982, supports Indian exporters and importers with finance.

questions.q: Insurance companies in India are regulated by the:
options: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)
National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)
questions.explain: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI), headquartered at Hyderabad, licenses and supervises insurers.

questions.q: Pension funds in India are regulated by the:
options: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA)
Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)
Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
questions.explain: The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) supervises pension schemes such as the National Pension System (NPS).

questions.q: In 1969, the Government of India nationalised how many major commercial banks?
questions.explain: Fourteen large banks were nationalised in 1969; six more followed in 1980.

questions.q: The largest public sector bank of India is the:
questions.explain: The State Bank of India (SBI) is India's biggest bank by assets, deposits and branches.

questions.q: The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), launched in 2014, is a scheme for:
options: Financial inclusion through zero-balance bank accounts
questions.explain: Under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), crores of people opened bank accounts, many with zero balance.

questions.q: The Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY) provides which type of insurance?
questions.explain: The Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY) gives life cover of two lakh rupees; the Suraksha Bima scheme covers accidents.

questions.q: The Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) provides which type of insurance?
questions.explain: The Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) gives accident cover at a very small annual premium.

questions.q: The Atal Pension Yojana (APY) is a pension scheme mainly meant for workers of the:
questions.explain: The Atal Pension Yojana (APY) promises a fixed monthly pension after the age of 60 to unorganised-sector workers.

questions.q: Under the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY), loans are given to:
questions.explain: MUDRA stands for Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency; its loans (Shishu, Kishore, Tarun) support tiny businesses.

questions.q: The Stand Up India scheme provides bank loans mainly to:
options: Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe and women entrepreneurs
questions.explain: Stand Up India helps Scheduled Caste (SC), Scheduled Tribe (ST) and women borrowers set up new (greenfield) enterprises.

questions.q: Ayushman Bharat — Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY) provides free health treatment cover per family per year of:
questions.explain: Under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY), eligible families get cashless hospitalisation cover of five lakh rupees a year.

questions.q: Under the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) scheme, eligible farmers receive income support of:
questions.explain: The Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) amount of six thousand rupees is paid in three instalments of two thousand rupees each.

questions.q: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) guarantees wage employment of at least:
options: 100 days per year to a rural household
questions.explain: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) guarantees 100 days of unskilled manual work to adult members of a rural household.

questions.q: The National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, later renamed after Mahatma Gandhi, was passed in the year:
questions.explain: The Act was passed in 2005 and work began in 2006 in the first set of districts.

questions.q: The Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) is a government scheme related to:
questions.explain: The Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) helps poor families build or upgrade houses, in both rural (Gramin) and urban areas.

questions.q: The Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) provides free Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) connections mainly to:
questions.explain: The Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY), launched in 2016 from Ballia, aimed to free poor women from smoky wood-fired stoves.

questions.q: The Swachh Bharat Mission (Clean India Mission) was launched on:
questions.explain: Launched on Mahatma Gandhi's birth anniversary in 2014, the Swachh Bharat Mission aimed at a clean India with toilets in every household.

questions.q: The Digital India programme, aimed at making government services available electronically, was launched in the year:
questions.explain: Digital India (2015) works on digital infrastructure, digital delivery of services and digital literacy.

questions.q: The 'Make in India' initiative, to encourage companies to manufacture in India, was launched in the year:
questions.explain: Make in India was launched in September 2014 to raise the share of manufacturing in the economy and create jobs.

questions.q: The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY), launched in 2016, is a scheme of:
questions.explain: The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) insures farmers against crop loss from drought, flood, hailstorm and pests.

questions.q: The Beti Bachao Beti Padhao scheme, for the survival, education and empowerment of the girl child, was launched in 2015 from:
questions.explain: The Beti Bachao Beti Padhao scheme was launched from Panipat, a district chosen because of its poor child sex ratio.
